symptom: A language cannot be enabled or disabled from MDL — `alter settings LANGUAGE` carries `DefaultLanguageCode` only, so the answer to "translate this app" was always "go to Studio Pro". Worse, `show languages` looks like the answer and is not: it lists languages that have TRANSLATIONS (from the catalog `strings` table), so a stock blank app reports **8** while **1** is enabled
cause: The enabled list (`Settings$LanguageSettings.Languages`) was read into the semantic model and never written: the settings overlay wrote `DefaultLanguageCode` and carried `Languages` through from the stored document. A handler could therefore report `Enabled language: ar_SD` and land **nothing** — the executor mutated `ps` and the writer dropped it on the floor
file: `mdl/grammar/domains/MDLSettings.g4` (`ADD`/`REMOVE` alternatives, `languageOptions`), `mdl/visitor/visitor_settings.go`, `mdl/executor/cmd_settings_languages.go`, and the write that makes it real: `mdl/settingsoverlay/settingsoverlay.go` (`Languages`, `Language`, `newLanguage`) wired from `mdl/backend/modelsdk/settings_write.go`
insight: Pin the element against a Studio Pro-authored reference before writing it — four things a guess gets wrong: the type is **`Texts$Language`** (not `Settings$…`) though it lives under `Settings$LanguageSettings`; there is **no `Description`** (Studio Pro derives "Arabic, Sudan" from `ar_SD`, so the code is the whole stored identity); Studio Pro **appends** rather than sorting; and **`CheckCompleteness` is stored `false` even for the default language**, whose Languages-table row reads "Yes" — the dialog says why ("the default language is always checked"), so that Yes is computed and writing `true` to match the UI produces a document Studio Pro never writes. Follow `settingsoverlay.ServerConfiguration`: match stored elements by their natural key, keep each one's document (so its `$ID` and any unmodelled property survive), derive a NEW element's shape from a sibling so no key is invented. **The refusal that was wrong:** removing a language does NOT delete its translations — the enabled list and the translation data are independent, which a stock app proves by enabling one language while storing translations in eight — so refusing on that basis would make the operation impossible on any project with a marketplace module and would assert something false about Mendix. Report the count instead. Verify by diffing the written element against the Studio Pro one field by field (identical here, `$ID` aside) and by checking the stored `$ID` of an untouched language survives. Example `mdl-examples/doctype-tests/languages.mdl`
